capabilities.name: Degraded Mode Operation
capabilities.notes: Baetyl supports 'temporary offline' computing and local node management (baetyl-core). It handles data synchronization with the cloud when connectivity is restored. However, specific logic for 'intermittent connectivity buffering' of GPS/telemetry streams as a primary gateway function is not explicitly detailed in the excerpts; it relies on the underlying application logic or K3s stateful sets.

capabilities.name: Encryption & Authentication
capabilities.notes: The MQTT link plugin explicitly requires 'certificate bidirectional authentication' (mTLS) for cloud connection. It parses node certificates and enforces TLS configuration. Secrets and Certificates are also managed by the Cloud Management Suite.

capabilities.name: Edge Application Runtime
capabilities.notes: Supports container and function (FaaS) application deployment on edge nodes via K3S/K8s or native mode.

capabilities.name: Device Shadow & Sync
capabilities.notes: Implements declarative design with Report/Desire shadows for data synchronization between edge and cloud.

capabilities.name: Node Management
capabilities.notes: Manages edge node lifecycle, activation, status collection, and application deployment.

description: Baetyl v2 is an open-source edge computing framework that extends cloud capabilities to edge devices. It manages applications (containers, functions) on edge nodes via K3S/K8s or native modes, handling device connection, message routing, OTA synchronization, and remote management. It serves as the foundational runtime for edge gateways but requires integration with specific IoT protocols and local buffering logic.
deployment_constraints: Requires K3S or Kubernetes for full feature set (Kube mode)
Requires mutual TLS certificates for cloud connection
known_gaps: No explicit evidence of built-in GPS/Telemetry aggregation logic; likely requires custom application deployment.
No explicit evidence of 'intermittent connectivity buffering' strategy beyond general offline support; specific QoS/drop policies not detailed.
Emergency Alert Ingestion (High Priority Topic) is not explicitly defined in the provided excerpts.
risks: Kube mode has high resource overhead (1GB RAM), which may be tight for constrained edge devices.
Native mode is under development and may lack stability or features compared to Kube mode.
Complexity of integrating custom IoT ingestion logic with the Baetyl runtime.
